metaDescription: Every lender in your statements by name, what each takes a month, how much of your income goes to EMIs, and which loan to close first.
title: EMIs and loans
intro: Every lender in your statements, by name: banks, NBFCs, loan apps and pay-later services. What each takes a month, what kind of loan it looks like, and which usually costs the most to keep.
none: No EMIs, loans or pay-later payments in your statements. Upload more months if you think something is missing.
tileLendersNote: Banks, NBFCs, apps and pay later
tileShareNote: Of about {income} a month that comes in regularly
tileShareUnknownNote: Shows once your salary repeats in your statements
tileBouncesNote: In the last 12 months of statements
band_ok: Comfortable: your EMIs take {percent} of your regular income, under 30%.
band_stretched: Stretched: your EMIs take {percent} of your regular income. Lenders usually want all EMIs under about 40 to 50%, so a new loan may be refused or cost more.
band_heavy: Heavy: your EMIs take {percent} of your regular income. One bad month can mean a bounced EMI, a fee and a mark on your credit score. Paying down the costliest loan first eases it fastest.
stackText: You are paying {count} pay-later services and loan apps at the same time. Paying one with another is how small amounts turn into a debt trap. Close the smallest first, and keep one at most.
closeIntro: If you have spare money, paying extra on the loan at the top usually saves the most. The order follows what each kind of loan usually costs; the actual rate is in your loan papers or the lender's app.
prepayNote: RBI does not allow banks and NBFCs to charge for closing or prepaying a floating-rate loan taken by an individual for a non-business purpose. For fixed-rate loans, check the foreclosure charge first.
borrowed: {amount} came in from this lender: most likely the loan itself.
lockedTitle: See every lender, and which to close first
lockedText: Subscribers see each lender by name, the kind of loan, how much of their income goes to EMIs, failed payments, and the order to close them in.
